pages.title: A09 · Deduplication and aggregates
lede: Objective (S3): perform deduplication and aggregate operations on DataFrames: count, approximate count distinct, mean, summary.
orders_cdc, a change data capture (CDC) feed, 8 rows: 5003 exact copy; 5001 24.00 -> 28.50 same day; 5002 30.00 -> 36.00 late (arrives Nov 4).

blocks.heading: 1. distinct and dropDuplicates
blocks.code:
orders_cdc.distinct().count()                         # 7  exact copies only (5003)
orders_cdc.dropDuplicates().count()                   # 7  same as distinct()
orders_cdc.dropDuplicates(["order_id"]).count()       # 5  one row per key, but WHICH row is not guaranteed
blocks.note: dropDuplicates has no sort argument (plan: first() per key). One local run kept 5001 24.00 + 5002 36.00, another kept 30.00. orderBy first is no guarantee.

blocks.heading: 2. Pick the business key
blocks.code:
orders_cdc.dropDuplicates(["customer_id"]).count()             # 4  too narrow: deletes real order 5001 or 5004
orders_cdc.dropDuplicates(["order_id", "change_ts"]).count()   # 7  too wide: updates survive
blocks.note: Business key = order_id. Not customer_id, not order_id + change_ts.

blocks.heading: 3. Keep the latest change with row_number
blocks.code:
w = Window.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy(F.col("change_ts").desc())
orders_latest = (orders_cdc.withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w))
                 .filter("rn = 1").drop("rn"))                     # 5 rows: 5001 28.50, 5002 36.00
-- SQL: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY change_ts DESC) AS rn ... WHERE rn = 1
blocks.note: Ties on change_ts? Add a tiebreaker column to orderBy. Streaming dropDuplicates keeps every key as state: use withWatermark().

blocks.heading: 4. Daily count and average order value (dedupe first)
blocks.note: Raw feed (wrong, no error): Nov 2 4 orders 29.63, Nov 3 4 orders 21.25. F.avg = F.mean, both skip NULLs.

pages.title: Counts, summary, checklist, snippet

blocks.heading: 5. count vs count_distinct vs approx_count_distinct
blocks.code:
F.count("*")                          # 8  rows, NULLs included (+1 NULL order_id row: 9)
F.count("order_id")                   # 8  non-NULL values (still 8 with the NULL row)
F.count_distinct("order_id")          # 5  exact, skips NULLs (= countDistinct)
F.approx_count_distinct("order_id")   # 5  estimate (HyperLogLog++), ~5% by default
blocks.note: rsd = max relative standard deviation, default 0.05. range(100000) local run: approx 95546, rsd 0.1 102065, exact 100000. Must be exact? count_distinct.

blocks.heading: 6. describe and summary
blocks.code:
orders_latest.select("amount").describe()   # count 5, mean 27.200000, stddev 11.35..., min 13.50, max 40.00
orders_latest.select("amount").summary()    # + 25% 18.0, 50% 28.5, 75% 36.0 (approximate)
blocks.note: Pick stats: summary("count", "mean", "min", "max"). summary is for exploration; use groupBy().agg() for reports.

blocks.heading: 7. Dedup checklist
blocks.text: 1) Business key: order_id. 2) Sort: change_ts (+ tiebreaker). 3) Keep latest: row_number, rn = 1; dropDuplicates(key) only for exact copies. 4) Check: count() after = count_distinct(key) before (5 = 5). 5) Then aggregate.

blocks.heading: 8. Reusable snippet: keep_latest
blocks.note: Memory trick: dropDuplicates keeps a row. row_number keeps the right row.

blocks.heading: Practice challenge
blocks.text: Q1 insert rows, dropDuplicates(): 5 (6 inserts, one exact copy). Q2 customer 101 total in orders_latest: 68.50 (28.50 + 40.00). Q3 count_distinct(customer_id): 4. Exam-style (exact distinct customers for an invoice): F.count_distinct("customer_id").
